sources.entry: Availability Calculator: Calculate how much downtime should be permitted in your SLA

summary.name: Availability Calculator
summary.one_liner: A reference page that converts availability percentages (90% to 99.999%) into allowed downtime per year, quarter, month, week, day and hour, for setting SLA or SLO targets.
summary.what_it_does: The page provides a table mapping availability levels from 90% to 99.999% to the downtime each level permits per year, quarter, month, week, day and hour. Values range from about 36.52 days per year at 90% down to about 5.26 minutes per year at 99.999%. It includes a quote from Ben Treynor arguing that 100% is not the right reliability target because users cannot tell 100% from 99.999%. The page is a static table with no input fields or interactive calculation described in the text.
notable: Covers availability levels from 90% to 99.999% in one table
Breaks downtime into year, quarter, month, week, day and hour
Listed in dastergon/awesome-sre under Service Level Agreement
caveats: Static reference table; the page text does not describe customizable inputs
Covers only availability percentages and does not model specific services or incident history
